how_to_read.one_value_per_report: Every field but marks_per_part is one value for the whole report. A test applied anywhere in the report is RAN; the test's name does not have to appear.
how_to_read.where_you_cannot_tell: null. A guess is worse than a gap: a gap is reported as unreadable, never as agreement.
how_to_read.closed_lists_are_closed: A field with 'values' takes one of them and nothing else.
how_to_read.never_counted: No field is added to another. No mark is a score. A count falsifies a prediction and settles nothing about a part.
how_to_read.sources: source='the report' means a marker reads it. source='the run record' means a program fills it from the transport's own record and the marker leaves it null.
how_to_read.certified_candidate: true when stage B can certify the field on the 96 reports in hand. P4.1 to P4.5 are read over certified fields only. false fields are read-outs and gauges and carry no arm difference.

agreement.field_and_document_rule: W3 section 7: 'A field agrees between two runs when the marker's record for the field is the same (RAN or not; the same mark on the same part; the same pairs named; the same rivals built; the same question kept) on the same document. Agreement is a count of documents, by field, never summed across fields or arms.'
agreement.per_kind: enum, int and bool agree when equal; a set agrees when the sets are equal; a map_enum agrees when the whole map is equal; text is never compared and is kept so a disagreement can be traced.
agreement.missing: A document where either side has no value is reported unreadable and named, never as agreement (testing-against-cases.md: "'Found nowhere' means unknown").
agreement.baseline_rule: W3 section 5, P4.1, word for word: 'For each certified field: the baseline is the number of documents on which any two of the three repeats of arm (a) disagree; the comparison is the number of documents on which any repeat of arm (a) disagrees with any repeat of arm (b). Falsified if, on any certified field, the comparison exceeds the baseline by more than two documents. A field whose baseline exceeds half the documents says nothing, and is reported so.'
agreement.k_rule: k = the arm's own (a)-to-(a) baseline on that field plus three (W3 P4.2; W10 section 5 fixes n = 8 documents, three repeats per box, tolerance two documents).
agreement.uninformative_rule: A field whose (a)-to-(a) baseline exceeds half the documents says nothing and is reported so; it carries no arm difference.
agreement.marker_to_marker_rule: The same per-kind rule, counted over reports, by field, never summed across fields or sets.
agreement.read_over: P4.1, P4.2, P4.3, P4.4, P4.5 and PA.3 are read over fields with certified_candidate true that stage B certified. P4.6 is read over modules_served alone. PA.1 and P4.9 are read from the run records, not from any marker's field.
agreement.cross_step_affordance: P4.2 and P4.3 are read over the cross-step fields that at least one of the eight arms documents affords. Which those are is instrument/affordance.json, field by field, from corpus/coverage.md and corpus/sources.json, with a line of reason for every document named. A cross-step field the corpus records as afforded by no arms document is not read (test_patches, which coverage.md section 7 states outright). A cross-step field the corpus records neither way is read, because 'found nowhere means unknown' and an exclusion needs evidence; agreement.py's 'never varies' flag is what would show such a field carried nothing. Added in the fix round, 22 September 2026, the reviewer's fault 18 and addendum W11 decision D4; marking-plan.md section 13.4. Round 3, 22 September 2026, the reviewer's fault 28: the table said this in its prose and not in its shape - it gave turned_own_test the same empty `affords` list it gives test_patches, and agreement.py reads the list, so a field the corpus records neither way was excluded with the reason 'no arms document affords it'. sorting.rule: W8 part B4, quoted: 'Fields whose work is done inside one step (a part's mark reached by remove, swap and poke) need only that step's material in the call's context. Fields whose object is the set of parts or the whole candidate (pairs that pull, the best rival, the same-explanation verdict, remove-in-groups) need a context that holds the parts together. The sorting is about what one call's context holds, not about whether a process persisted; it is written before any run and is not re-sorted on the reports that break it.'
sorting.the_line_drawn: Cross-step is a field whose object is the set of parts of the explanation, or the whole candidate. Within-step is a field a call can reach from one part and one step's material. B4 names three within-step tests (remove, swap, poke) and W3 P3.5 confirms them ('they are dropped from the within-step set for phase 4 and remove carries it alone').
sorting.the_pull_named: W8 section 6, builder B: 'B4 against B12: the more fields called cross-step, the more arm (d) is predicted to lose, and the easier P4.3 passes for a reason other than partition; the line is drawn at fields phase 3 certified whose object is the set of parts.' So shape is within-step: a final call handed a pile of answers can write all seven of its elements from that pile. What would show the line in the wrong place: arm (d) losing shape while keeping every cross-step field.

three_layers.rule: Plan 52, quoted: 'A report can be wrong in three places, and the marks must say which. 1. The document. What it actually says. Checked against the text. 2. The skill. What its words told the reader to do. 3. The reader. ... A finding contradicted by the document is the reader's fault unless the skill's wording pushed it there; only then is it the skill's. The marker must name which, in one line, every time.'

fields.name: test_pull
fields.title: Pull
fields.criterion: Plan 52's rule kept, with one case added in the fix round on 22 September 2026 (the reviewer's fault 3; the addendum is marking-plan.md section 13.1). H64 put this test's agreement at 45 of 48. RAN in either of two cases. (i) The report says of two things in the explanation that making one stronger makes the other weaker, and says which gives way, or where the line is, or what would show the line drawn in the wrong place. (ii) The report names both sides of a tension between two things in the explanation - two things it presents as pulling against each other, competing, or in tension over one job, and not merely as different - and says which gives way, or where the line is, or what would show the line drawn in the wrong place; the stronger-weaker wording need not appear. A report that says the line is not drawn ('Nothing marks where the vapour regime ends and the solid regime begins') has said where the line is, in the same way that 'no gauge is offered' is the patches test run. NAME ONLY when a tension is asserted with neither side named, or when both sides are named and nothing is said about which gives way, where the line is, or what would show the line drawn in the wrong place. ABSENT when the report names no tension between two things in the explanation. CANNOT takes the general three-part form. The two things need not be items of the report's own part list; when they are not, this field is still RAN and pairs_that_pull is empty. What case (ii) gives up: a report that only contrasts two parts and says which the text favours is now RAN, so RAN no longer tells a report that asked the stronger-weaker question from one that reported a contrast with a winner; pairs_that_pull records the pair and quotes keeps the sentence, which is where that difference stays visible.

fields.name: shape_elements
fields.title: The seven elements of a full report
fields.criterion: H64 struck shape's PART boundary ('34 of 48 agree, and every disagreement is the second marker saying PART where the first said NONE ... or FULL'). The written rule that replaces it: do not judge the shape; fill these seven, each Y or N, and the shape follows by the rule in the shape field. E1 the question frozen: the report says in one place what is being explained and what is asked. E2 the parts listed: a numbered or bulleted list of the parts of the explanation. E3 the jobs listed: a list of the things the explanation has to account for, set out apart from the parts; naming where the jobs came from is not a jobs list. E4 the change list: the report gathers, in one place, the changes it ranges over, or says what the change list leaves out. E5 tests run: at least one of the eleven applied with a concrete change or a named neighbour. E6 a mark on every part: every part in E2's list carries one of the eight marks. E7 the report's sections: the method's seven report sections are present and in its order, each doing its work, whatever they are called.

fields.name: marks_per_part
fields.title: The eight marks, part by part
fields.criterion: New field (W3 P3.2). One entry per part. THE KEY, as the fix round fixed it on 22 September 2026 (the reviewer's fault 4; marking-plan.md section 13.2): take the part's label from the report's part-by-part section - the table or list that gives each part its mark - where there is one, and otherwise from the report's parts list; then normalise it. To normalise: take the characters up to the first space, '(' or '['; strip from each end of that token every character that is not a letter or a digit; use what is left as the key when it is label-shaped, that is at most two letters followed by at most two digits ('A', 'H', 'P3', 'P10', 'iv'); otherwise use the whole label as the report writes it, trimmed, with the same stripping at each end ('Time is a fourth dimension'). The rule is written so that the two lists one report commonly carries - '**A.** Time is a fourth dimension' in the parts list and 'A (time = 4th dimension)' in the marks table - give one key and not two. A row that covers two parts under one label ('P3, P4 decomposition and ratio') is one entry under that label's normalised key. TWO CLAUSES ADDED IN ROUND 2 OF THE FIX ROUND (22 September 2026, the reviewer's fault 4, held open after round 1; marking-plan.md section 14.1), because the rule as it stood gave one key to two different parts in seven of the record's ninety-six reports. (1) A TOKEN IS LABEL-SHAPED ONLY WHERE IT STANDS AS AN ENUMERATOR. The label must not begin with a quotation mark of any kind (" “ ” ' ‘ ’ «), and what follows the token's last letter or digit inside the label must be at least one character that is not a letter or a digit — the separator — and then at least one more letter or digit — the rest of the label. So 'P3 the sum', '**A.** Time is a fourth dimension', 'A (time = 4th dimension)', 'H, exact images' and 'iv) the third premise' all key to their enumerator, and '"a mathematical line... has no real existence"', '"I don't, for certain, know which"' and '"To capture these advances… necessitated an update"' do not key to 'a', 'I' and 'To' but keep the whole label. A label that is a bare token with nothing after it ('P1', 'A') is not an enumerator either, and the whole-label rule gives back the same string, so nothing moves. (2) THE KEY IS UNIQUE WITHIN ONE REPORT. Where two or more rows of the part-by-part section normalise to the same key, each of those rows — and only those rows — keeps its whole label as the report writes it, trimmed and end-stripped by the same stripping; a row that did not collide keeps its normalised key. So 'A, specific 4-D content' and 'A, "jargon + named pushback"' are two entries and not one, and 'B.' and 'B′.' likewise. The criterion says both clauses out loud because a marker must apply them, and pairs_that_pull inherits them. THE VALUE is the one of the eight marks the report gives that part. Match the longest mark first, so 'held if' is read before 'held'. Extra words around a mark do not change it: 'Held, but coarser than stated' is held; 'Held, catch-all with a gauge' is held; 'Loose, ungauged catch-all' is loose. A part whose mark cell contains two or more different marks of the eight is left out of the map and its cell is copied into quotes. A part with no mark is left out. Read by document, never summed.

fields.criterion: New field (W3 P3.2). One member per pair the report names as pulling against each other, written 'A|B', where A and B are two different part keys of the report, normalised exactly as marks_per_part's key rule normalises them, in the order the report writes them. THE KEYS ARE marks_per_part's KEYS AND THIS FIELD INHERITS BOTH CLAUSES ADDED TO THEM IN ROUND 2 OF THE FIX ROUND (22 September 2026, the reviewer's fault 4; marking-plan.md section 14.1): a token is label-shaped only where it stands as an enumerator, and a key that would collide with another row's inside one report is replaced, for the colliding rows only, by the whole label trimmed and end-stripped. Where a colliding row's key is a whole label, the member carries that whole label on that side, so a pull named on a report whose keys collide is written with the long keys and not with the short ones. A PULL NAMED BETWEEN TWO GROUPS of the report's own parts (the fix round, 22 September 2026, the reviewer's fault 4; marking-plan.md section 13.2) gives ONE MEMBER PER CROSS PAIR: for 'A-C ... D and G' the members are A|D, A|G, B|D, B|G, C|D, C|G, the left of each member taken from the side the report names first. A side written as a range ('A-C', 'P1-P3', with any dash) means every part of the report's own list from the first named to the last named inclusive, in the order that list runs; a side written as a list ('D and G', 'P2, P4') means the parts it names. A side that is not written as an explicit range or list of the report's own part labels - a description such as 'the argument parts' - cannot be expanded: the pull is not a member, the sentence goes in quotes, and test_pull still records that the test ran. A tension named between things that are not in the report's part list is not a member and goes in quotes; the test_pull field still records that the test ran. A part said to pull against itself is not a member. The empty set is a value and means the report names no pair; use null only when you cannot tell whether a sentence names a pair.

fields.name: rivals_built
fields.title: Rivals built, named
fields.criterion: New field (W3 P3.2). One member per rival the report builds. A rival is built when the report states it in a sentence of its own and either names a change that would tell it from the explanation under test or says plainly that no change on the change list can. A rival only named is not a member and goes in quotes. HOW A MEMBER IS WRITTEN (the fix round, 22 September 2026, the reviewer's fault 5; marking-plan.md section 13.3): the report's own short name for the rival where it gives one, lowercased and trimmed, with any quotation marks round it removed and any punctuation at either end of what is left dropped (so a name quoted with the sentence's full stop inside the quotation marks, "some sleight-of-hand trick.", is written 'some sleight-of-hand trick'); otherwise the first five words of the sentence that states the rival, lowercased and trimmed, each word as the report writes it, with punctuation at a word's edge dropped. The report gives a short name of its own when the sentence that states the rival carries a phrase that names the rival as a thing - a noun phrase, with no verb of its own inside it - in quotation marks or otherwise set off as the rival's name ('some sleight-of-hand trick'). A quoted phrase with a verb in it ('he built a machine, don't ask how') states the rival and does not name it, so the five-word rule applies. The sentence that states the rival is the first sentence in which the rival is put, and its words are its whitespace-separated tokens counted from that sentence's first word. THREE CLAUSES ADDED IN ROUND 2 OF THE FIX ROUND (22 September 2026, the reviewer's fault 25; marking-plan.md section 14.2), because the rule as round 1 left it was not decidable on reports neither A4 nor the reviewer had named. (1) WHERE THE SENTENCE STARTS. A lead-in that names the test is not part of the sentence: any list marker ('-', '*', '1.'), and then any run set in bold, italics, brackets or parentheses whose text carries the word 'rival' or 'rivals' ('**Rival.**', '- **Best rival.**', '**Rivals:**', '**Rival explanation.**'), together with the punctuation and the space that close it. The sentence's first word is the first word after that run, so the five words are counted from there and never from the lead-in: '**Rival explanation.** Drop the Fourth-Dimension argument for a bare …' gives 'drop the fourth-dimension argument for' and never 'rival explanation drop the fourth-dimension'. (2) WHICH SENTENCE. 'The first sentence in which the rival is put' is the first sentence of the report's own whole-explanation section — the section that runs file 33's whole-explanation checks (flip, reverse, hunt the answer in the starting points, add a job, build the best rival, pull, check the patches, look inside) — that states that rival. A mention in a part-by-part cell is not it: the cell goes in quotes, and a rival the report states only in a part-by-part cell and nowhere in the whole-explanation section is not a member. Where the report has no whole-explanation section, it is the first sentence of the report outside the part-by-part section that states the rival; that last clause is the instrument's and not the reviewer's, and is here so that the rule reaches a report of any shape. (3) TWO RIVALS IN ONE SENTENCE. Where one sentence states two or more rivals, each takes the report's own noun phrase for it as its name, written by the naming rule above, whether or not that phrase is quoted or otherwise set off: "Benioff's machine and Feynman's simulator are the near neighbours" gives 'benioff's machine' and 'feynman's simulator', and 'The dissent, and *Phelps*.' gives 'the dissent' and 'phelps'. Where the sentence gives no noun phrase for them, THE FIELD IS NULL FOR THAT REPORT and the sentence goes in quotes, rather than two rivals collapsing into one five-word member. The empty set is a value.

fields.criterion: Plan 52's three-layer rule, on every report: 'A finding contradicted by the document is the reader's fault unless the skill's wording pushed it there; only then is it the skill's. The marker must name which, in one line, every time.' For this round layer 2 is the thing under test: the skill's words together with the arm's arrangement. 'none' when the report contains nothing the marker can fault. It is not certified and carries no arm difference, because it is the marker's own attribution and a difference on it would be a difference between markers.

example.quote: | P7 | fixed | the owner set it.

fitting.quote: | P7 | fixed | the owner set it.
fitting.why: The fault is the skill's wording, not the reader's care: H64 traces it to the two-list collision, 'the eight part-marks ... and the provenance words ... are two closed lists in the same style, and "nothing in the skill says the two vocabularies must not be mixed"'. Both markers of H63 judged this use of fixed improper.

fitting.quote: P8 the Psychologist's "presentation below the threshold… diluted presentation"
fitting.why: The document gives the phrase to the Time Traveller. Nothing in the skill's wording pushes a reader to reassign a quotation, so under plan 52's rule the layer is the reader.

fields.name: layer_at_fault_line
fields.title: The one line that names the layer
fields.criterion: One line: what the fault is, and why it sits at the layer named. Where the layer is the thing under test, the line quotes the sentence of file 33 that pushed the reader there; plan 52's trap, kept: 'Recording a break without quoting the line of the skill that caused it.' Never compared.

stage_B_certification.rule: W10 stage B: 'No field carries an arm difference in stage C unless it agreed here.'

thresholds_from_W3.P3.1: Of the three fields H64 struck (shape, turned_own_test, same_explanation), at least two agree on at least 44 of 48. Fewer than two, and the cross-step fields cannot carry an arm difference; stage C runs on the certified fields and the two marker-free read-outs alone, and says so.
thresholds_from_W3.P3.2: The three new fields (marks_per_part, pairs_that_pull, rivals_built) each agree on at least 40 of 48 on first marking, marks_per_part read by document. Fewer, and that field is kept as quotes only, as H64 kept the verdict.
thresholds_from_W3.P3.3: question_identity agrees on at least 46 of 48.
thresholds_from_W3.P3.4: At most one field needs a second rewording. Two or more and the phase stops and reports the patches with what each gave up.
thresholds_from_W3.P3.5: test_swap and test_poke each agree on at least 42 of 48. Otherwise they leave the within-step set for stage C and test_remove carries it alone.

threshold_added_here.which: the eight other tests, remove_in_groups, modules_self_reported, attributions, shape_elements
threshold_added_here.rule: 39 of 48, which is 80 percent, the only number the record fixes for a test field (H63 prediction 2, borne out at 84 percent of the 528 cells).
threshold_added_here.marked: This number is the instrument's own addition, not W3's. Without it a field agreeing on 20 of 48 could carry an arm difference, which is worse. What would show it wrong: a field that agrees on 38 of 48 in stage B and on which every arm difference in stage C is larger than its own (a)-to-(a) baseline by more than the tolerance, which would mean a struck field was carrying real signal.

stage_B_certification.what_is_struck: A field below its threshold is struck from carrying an arm difference in stage C. It is still marked, and its quotes are kept, and it is named in the results file. If every cross-step candidate is struck, P4.2 and P4.3 are unreadable and stage C runs on the marker-free read-outs alone (W3 P3.1). If test_swap and test_poke fall below 42 of 48, the within-step set is test_remove, shape, shape_elements, marks_per_part, question_identity, modules_self_reported and attributions, and P4.4 is read on those. A field whose (a)-to-(a) baseline in stage C exceeds half the documents says nothing, whatever stage B said.

asks_of_the_harness: first_marker.py builds its prompt from every field; the fields with source 'the run record' must be left out of the prompt and filled at collect from the run record, or every marker returns null on five fields.

agreement.py reads P4.1 to P4.5 over every comparable field; it must read them over fields with certified_candidate true only, or modules_served, marks_outside_closed_list and layer_at_fault carry arm differences they are not evidence for.
first_marker.py validate must also check that shape follows from shape_elements by this file's rule, and that every key of marks_per_part appears in the report.

agreement.py must read instrument/affordance.json, read P4.2 and P4.3 over the cross-step fields that at least one of the eight arms documents affords, and flag a field that never varies across every run of every arm as 'never varies' beside its 'uninformative' flag; a field so flagged carries no arm difference. Added in the fix round, 22 September 2026 (the reviewer's fault 18, addendum W11 decision D4). Round 3 (fault 28) adds what 'the fields at least one arms document affords' does not cover: a cross-step field affordance.json does not name is READ, not excluded, and only a field named there with an empty `affords` list is left out. agreement.py already did this and was not changed. marks.affordance now appends affordance.json's `note_to_the_counts_file` to the string the counts file prints as `corpus_affordance_from`, so the counts file says which of fault 28's two moves was made; the note carries no decision and changes no count.

addenda.round: the fix round of plan W10 stage A, under addendum W11
addenda.changed: A second RAN case added: both sides of a tension named, and which gives way (or where the line is, or what would show the line drawn in the wrong place), without the stronger-weaker clause. NAME ONLY extended to both sides named with none of those three said, and ABSENT stated, so that every report shape reaches one of the four values.
addenda.gives_up: RAN no longer tells a report that asked the stronger-weaker question from one that reported a contrast with a winner; pairs_that_pull and quotes are where that difference stays visible.

addenda.round: the fix round of plan W10 stage A, under addendum W11
addenda.changed: The part key is fixed by rule (the marks table first, else the parts list; normalised to the leading token where that token is label-shaped, else the whole label), and a pull named between two groups of the report's own parts gives one member per cross pair.
addenda.gives_up: A key that is not the report's own words; and a set that grows with the size of the two groups, which two markers must match member for member.

addenda.round: the fix round of plan W10 stage A, under addendum W11
addenda.changed: A written naming rule: the report's own short name where it gives one, otherwise the first five words of the sentence that states the rival, lowercased and trimmed. Punctuation at either end of a name is dropped: found by running the rule on the frozen fitting report, which returned 'some sleight-of-hand trick.' with the sentence's full stop and so would have moved a frozen value.
addenda.gives_up: A member that reads as a name; two rivals stated in sentences with the same first five words would collide into one member.

addenda.round: the fix round of plan W10 stage A, under addendum W11
addenda.changed: instrument/affordance.json added: for every cross-step field, which of the eight arms documents afford it, from corpus/coverage.md and corpus/sources.json, with a line of reason each; and the rule that P4.2 and P4.3 are read over the cross-step fields at least one arms document affords, with a fourth ask of the harness.
addenda.gives_up: test_patches carries no arm difference this round; the reserve is not raided to give it purchase (W3 section 8, addendum W11 decision D4).

addenda.round: round 2 of the fix round of plan W10 stage A, under addendum W11
addenda.changed: Two clauses that make the key unique. A token is label-shaped only where it stands as an enumerator (a separator and more text after it, and the label does not begin with a quotation mark); and where two rows of one report's part-by-part section still normalise alike, those rows keep their whole label, trimmed and end-stripped. pairs_that_pull inherits both.
addenda.gives_up: A key that is short and uniform: on the seven reports of the ninety-six where keys collided, the colliding rows now carry long keys and their neighbours carry short ones, so one report's map mixes the two shapes; and a row's key now depends on which other rows the marker read as part of the part-by-part section.

addenda.round: round 2 of the fix round of plan W10 stage A, under addendum W11
addenda.changed: Three clauses: a bold or bracketed lead-in naming the test is not part of the sentence; the sentence is the first one in the report's own whole-explanation section that states the rival, and a part-by-part cell is not it; and where one sentence states two or more rivals each takes the report's own noun phrase for it, the field being null where the sentence gives none.
addenda.gives_up: Two rivals the report gives no noun phrase for now make the whole field null, so a report that built two rivals and named neither counts as unreadable rather than as one member; and the whole-explanation section must be identified before the field can be filled, which a report that does not use file 33's report shape makes a judgement.

addenda.round: round 3 of the fix round of plan W10 stage A, under addendum W11
addenda.field: none - the cross-step set P4.2 and P4.3 are read over (no criterion changed)
addenda.changed: instrument/affordance.json stops naming a cross-step field the corpus records neither way: turned_own_test leaves `fields` for `fields_the_corpus_does_not_record` and carries no `affords` key, so the harness's standing rule ('a field the table does not name is read, not excluded') reaches it and P4.2 and P4.3 are read over twelve certified cross-step fields instead of eleven. An empty `affords` list in the table now means one thing only: the corpus records that no arms document affords the field (test_patches). marks.affordance gained four lines that pass the table's own one-sentence note through to the counts file; agreement.py is unchanged.
addenda.gives_up: The table no longer has a row for every cross-step field, so the round-1 check 'fourteen fields, fourteen rows, none missing' is replaced by 'every cross-step field stands in one of the two lists and none in both'; and a later editor who deletes a row by accident now makes the field read rather than making the harness complain, which the two-list check is the gauge against.
addenda.no_field_reworded: No criterion, kind, sort, values or certified_candidate moved; turned_own_test's criterion is word for word what W10-A4-1 froze. W3 P3.4's rewording count does not move.
